solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: European carried by rail coming to Paddington, say

indicators.note: a thing carried by something sits inside it, so the rail holds the European

parts.note: a bar is a rail, as on a fence or a towel rail

explanation.surface: A European passenger arrives by train at London's Paddington station.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington looks like the London railway station, which the rail sets up; it is Paddington Bear of the children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is a famous fictional bear, so he is an example of the animal.

clue.text: Pieced together picture of ancient lawgiver

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an image made from small fitted tiles
second meaning: relating to Moses, the lawgiver of the Old Testament

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective formed from Moses is the same word as the tiled picture, so the clue reads like a description of one artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiled artwork is assembled from small pieces, and the adjective for Moses's law shares the spelling.

clue.text: Misbehaving youngster, intermittently aberrant

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then, so every other letter of aberrant is used

parts.note: the letters in second, fourth, sixth and eighth place of aberrant are used

explanation.surface: A naughty child behaves badly from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilt, badly behaved child is commonly called this, a mildly insulting synonym.

clue.text: Caught, unfortunately, outside one Channel port

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps around it, so the regret word surrounds the one

parts.note: alas is the exclamation of regret, the sense of unfortunately
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is sadly stranded beyond a ferry port across the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: This French town is the main ferry harbour on the English Channel crossing from Dover.

clue.text: I pardon a wrong, harbouring unreasonable suspicions

indicators.note: letters set wrong are put in the wrong order, so these get rearranged

parts.note: these three words supply the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone forgives an offence while still feeling distrustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A wrong' reads as the thing being pardoned, but wrong is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suffering irrational distrust of others is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Politically co-operative oil company retaining current skilled worker

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so the company's letters hold the current

parts.note: BP is the British oil company, formerly British Petroleum
I is the physics symbol for electric current
an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: An oil firm keeps an electrician on staff in a spirit of cross-party cooperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement or support from both main parties is described with this adjective.

clue.text: On course, performing relatively well or rather poorly?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on a golf course, a score under the standard is a good one
second meaning: slightly unwell or not up to the usual standard

explanation.walkthrough: In golf a lower score is better, so the phrase that means good play also means feeling unwell; the question mark flags the contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf idiom for scoring under standard doubles as everyday slang for being off-colour or unwell.

clue.text: Flamboyancy Scrabble player can never produce

definitions.meaning: the meaning of the word: dash, vivacity, flair
a Scrabble set holds only one tile of the letter needed four times here, plus one blank

explanation.walkthrough: The game has a single Z tile and two blanks, so a word needing four Zs can never be laid down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means vitality and stylish flair, a synonym for flamboyance.

clue.text: Jack's appearing in operatic part in Lawrence's place

indicators.note: something appearing in another is placed within it, so the sailor sits inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, and AB is an able-bodied seaman; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A singer named Jack takes a role in an opera set where Lawrence lived.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence is T. E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia'.
explanation.definitionFit: T. E. Lawrence's famous epithet ties him to this peninsula region where he fought in the desert revolt.

clue.text: Some tigers at zoo not the real thing

indicators.note: only some of these words' letters are used, a run sitting inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of tigers, all of at and the start of zoo

explanation.surface: Certain tigers kept in a zoo are not truly wild.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an inferior substitute or imitation, artificial rather than genuine.

clue.text: Rip off, in a word, someone who's reckless

parts.note: to tear is to rip
away means off, as in 'go away'

explanation.surface: Telling someone to strip something away, plainly, describes a wild youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a word' tells you the two-word phrase for rip off is written as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, impetuous young person, often a delinquent, is called this in British English.

clue.text: For example, football magazine's linked with Liverpool, say

parts.note: The Spectator is a British weekly magazine; with the possessive it gives the S
Liverpool is a major English seaport, an example of a port

explanation.surface: A magazine's coverage connects with Liverpool Football Club.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool suggests the football club, which fits the definition, but here it is the city as a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Football is watched by large crowds, the classic example of a game for onlookers.

clue.text: Kind of author that takes gamble with flier, originally

parts.note: to play is to gamble, as in playing the tables
the Wright brothers were the original aviators, making the first powered flight

explanation.surface: An author risks a wager with a pioneering aviator.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes dramas for the stage is a particular sort of writer.

clue.text: Final notice about monarch's round-the-world trip

indicators.note: one word goes about another when it surrounds it, so the death notice encloses the monarch

parts.note: an obituary, OBIT, is a final notice of someone's life
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: An obituary describes a sovereign's journey around the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: A path circling the Earth, as a satellite makes, is a trip around the world.

clue.text: Island with a lot of dance

definitions.text: Island with a lot of dance

indicators.note: with means the island letter is added alongside the dance
a lot of a word is most of it, so the dance loses its last letter

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An island known for its abundance of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a fair description: the Indonesian island is famous for its traditional temple dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indonesian island is celebrated for its elaborate traditional dance performances.

clue.text: Islander's at home, nursing his arm that's broken

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the home word cradles the jumble

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: a broken thing is rearranged, so his arm gets jumbled

parts.note: these two words supply the six letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A man from an island is home, cradling his broken arm.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Islander is 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Ireland is an inhabitant of an island, so he is an islander.

clue.text: What's repeatedly found in grizzly bear, possibly, or other wild animal

parts.note: the letter appearing twice in grizzly is Z

indicators.note: possibly points to a possible arrangement of bear's letters

parts.note: the four letters of bear are the ones to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The puzzle-like question asks what turns up in a grizzly bear or another wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped African horse is a wild animal, set apart here from the bear.

clue.text: Not for touching

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as 'not suitable for touching', but they split into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means both opposed to and in physical contact with, as in leaning a ladder on a wall.

clue.text: Flamboyance — it's not a word that can be seen in this clue

definitions.text: it's not a word that can be seen in this clue
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the punctuation mark printed after Flamboyance

explanation.walkthrough: The long punctuation mark in the clue is not a word, yet it names the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both stylish panache and the horizontal punctuation line printed in the clue.

clue.text: Western crew showering after time for strenuous exercise

indicators.note: showering comes after time, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
raining is coming down in showers

explanation.surface: A rowing crew from the west takes showers after their session of hard exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: Showering suggests washing after a workout; here it is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting barbells and dumbbells to build strength is a demanding form of physical workout.

clue.text: Sporting and jovial male also having aesthetic interests

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
arty means showily interested in the arts

explanation.surface: A sporty, cheerful man also has artistic tastes.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a bluff, boisterous and cheerful manner, often of a sporty type.

clue.text: Insignificant type's critical comment on wine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person of no importance
second meaning: '...', a taster's complaint that a wine is thin

explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the word is a wine critic's verdict that the drink lacks fullness; 's after type is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance is described with this word, while a thin wine lacks fullness of flavour.

clue.text: Wrongly perceived young woman in front of crowd, speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the result is judged by how it sounds when said

parts.words: young woman in front of crowd
parts.note: a miss is a young woman, placed in front of a herd, which is a crowd

explanation.surface: A young woman addressing a crowd is wrongly perceived.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS HERD, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishear something is to catch it wrongly, perceiving the sound incorrectly.

clue.text: Blue swallow

explanation.walkthrough: Blue looks like a colour and swallow like a bird, but they are a mood and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both low in spirits and to drink something quickly in one go.

clue.text: Interfere with person who's entitled to hold key

indicators.note: one word held by another sits inside it, so the aristocrat contains the key

parts.note: a noble is an aristocrat holding a title
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A meddler tampers with someone who believes they have a right to keep a key.
explanation.walkthrough: Entitled means having a title, not feeling deserving.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamper with a racehorse or bribe someone improperly, so as to influence an outcome, is to meddle with it.

clue.text: Be first to play heavy metal? Doesn't sound like it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to play first in a card game or go ahead
second meaning: the soft dense element Pb

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses share spelling but not pronunciation, as the tail comment admits; heavy metal is the element, not the rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to go first and also names the dense grey metal once used in pipes.

clue.text: Scotch is what drunken revellers try, initially

indicators.note: a drunken word staggers out of order, so what is rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of what are the ones to be rearranged

indicators.note: only the opening letters of revellers and try are taken

parts.note: the first letters of these two words are taken

explanation.surface: Scotch whisky is what tipsy partygoers attempt to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like whisky, which drunken revellers suit, but it is the verb meaning to put a stop to.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to foil or frustrate it, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Remove two wives, with a third mistreated inside

indicators.note: the jumble goes inside the pair of wives

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife, taken twice

indicators.note: mistreated letters are handled roughly and rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bigamist who mistreats a third wife among them should be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back or pull out something, as an offer or troops, is to remove it.
